# Baize -- migration inventory and derivation

The AC-10.3 pattern, third application: every entry in Baize's `bin/.devbin/config.yaml` and every handler under `cmd/` is DERIVED from the launcher it replaces, via this document. Read the old side (`bin/baize`, `bin/baize_*`, `bin/bz`, `bin/cli`, `bin/repl` -- 2,683 lines, 2026-08-09) before writing anything on the new side.

## The old surface

15 commands (`BAIZE_COMMANDS` in `bin/baize_helpers`): `server iex repl cli test check which cv perf db fmt docs publish build version`. Shared options parsed in every handler: `--env dev|test|prod` -> MIX_ENV (unknown value refused), `--json` -> ARCA_STYLE=json, `--iex` -> BAIZE_IEX=true. Project env: `export_config_path` (BAIZE_CONFIG_PATH=.baize, set-if-unset). Version: the VERSION file is the ONE home (devbin's default `version_from`), mix.exs derives from it at compile time, no sidecars. Umbrella with ONE child app (`rack`); the load-bearing distinction is `rack_task` (in-process `mix do --app rack`, routine only) vs `rack_task_sub` (`cd apps/rack && mix`, a REAL subprocess -- mandatory for anything that can meet a fresh DB, because the in-process form silently skips migrations, and the deprecated `mix cmd --app` spelling must not come back). Seals: `tmp/test/<stamp>.{mix,credo}.{out,errors}` + LATEST pointers, lowercase suffix family. Stubs refuse via `not_yet` -- reason + gating condition, **exit 3** -- and `test all` reports rc-3 gates as SKIPPED, keyed on the exit code, never as passed.

## Command dispositions

| Old                           | New                             | Kind                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `baize server`                | `cmd/server`                    | Thin handler: the AGENT BAN (CLAUDECODE/CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID present and BAIZE_ALLOW_SERVER!=1 -> die; the authored guard-rail), the :4800 banner, BAIZE_IEX -> `iex -S mix phx.server`.                 |
| `baize iex`                   | `cmd/iex`                       | Thin handler: export_config_path + `exec iex -S mix`. Catalogue row lacks the config-store env.                                                                                                           |
| `baize repl`                  | `cmd/repl`                      | Thin handler: config store + rlwrap_exec with Baize's real paths -- completions `bin/completions/completions.txt` (builtin assumes `repl.txt`), history BAIZE_REPL_HISTORY -> `mix baize.cli repl`.        |
| `baize cli`                   | `cmd/cli`                       | Thin handler: first-arg -h intercept -> help topic, config store, `exec mix baize.cli "$@"`.                                                                                                              |
| `baize test mix`              | `cmd/test.d/mix`                | Full port of the glyph-feed sealed runner onto lib/runlog: wrapper flags --verbose/--with-errors --no-out --out-dir --purge --purge-only --allow-empty --no-trace --no-color --report/--no-report, the umbrella per-suite REPORT TABLE, the MIX_ENV=test contradiction refusal, the compile/boot tail, the zero-test promotion Baize originated. Suffix -> MIX. Grammar: byte-compared IDENTICAL to devbin's (the shipped grammar carries the umbrella headers -- corpus lineage), so `grammar_for mix`; the predicted divergence did not exist. |
| `baize test credo`            | `cmd/test.d/credo`              | Same shape: `mix credo --strict`, Checking-N zero promotion + --allow-empty. Suffix -> CREDO.                                                                                                              |
| `baize test shell`            | `cmd/test.d/shell`              | Near-verbatim port. DELIBERATELY UNSEALED (the authored ruling: its verdict is its own exit status, and sealing it would put this gate behind the machinery it exists to check). The `BAIZE_SHELL_SENTINEL_DIR` env name is the contract with `test/shell/support/assert.sh` -- KEPT. |
| `baize test rust`             | `cmd/test.d/rust`               | STUB, exit 3 with the gating condition (ST0005 Phase 3), ported verbatim in the `not_yet` shape.                                                                                                           |
| `baize test suite <name>`     | `cmd/test` (suite branch)       | The named-suite map (marker/games/cockatoo/perf/domain/web) -- suite_path's one executable home moves whole; the `-d` guard (a moved suite fails loudly) comes with it. Resolves and hands to test.d/mix.  |
| `baize test all [--full]`     | `cmd/test` (all branch)         | credo + shell + rust, mix OPT-IN behind --full (hv's standing "never the bare full suite" rule, ENFORCED here); rc-3 -> SKIPPED bucket; continue past breach. WIDENED to also fan --purge/--purge-only/--allow-empty to the runners (hv's fleet ruling 2026-08-09); everything else still refused. |
| bare `baize test` / `-h`      | `cmd/test`                      | Help topic, **exit 0** -- Baize's shape (Laksa's bare-test-exits-2 ruling is Laksa's, not the fleet's).                                                                                                    |
| `baize check compile`         | config override                 | Old runs `rack_task_sub compile --warnings-as-errors --force` -- the umbrella SUBPROCESS form, full build (the only type gate; no Dialyzer). Catalogue row runs plain `mix compile ...` at root. `run: cmd/.lib/check-compile`, grammar mix + log COMPILE restated.  |
| `baize check format`          | catalogue @builtin              | One arm per declared language; with `languages: [elixir, shell]` that is exactly `mix format --check-formatted` (shell has no fmt arm) -- old parity.                                                     |
| `baize check deps`            | catalogue row                   | `mix deps.unlock --check-unused` -- exact match, no entry.                                                                                                                                                |
| `baize check toolchain`       | catalogue @builtin              | Both are two-arm pin-vs-active with the same anchored parse, the same -otp suffix strip, the same full-OTP_VERSION read and the same said-out-loud coarse fallback. Output format differs; verdict semantics identical. Baize has NO Dockerfile -- the image arm does not exist here (a data point for AC-11.11: not a corpus norm). |
| `baize check critic`          | catalogue @builtin              | Byte-for-byte the same logic (declared-intent-langs x headless, --staged default, empty-staging warning). Baize's intent config declares elixir+swift+rust+shell; all four have headless critics; both sides run all four.  |
| `baize check credo`           | config row                      | Old DELEGATES to the sealed credo runner (one `mix credo` home; the ic false-"gates clean" lesson in its header). `run: cmd/.lib/check-credo` -> re-enters `devbin test credo`; grammar credo, log CREDO.  |
| `baize check all`             | synthesised                     | Old order: toolchain format deps compile critic credo. New: declared rows first (compile, credo), then catalogue actives (format, deps, toolchain, critic). Coverage identical (six gates); ORDER differs -- recorded as a deliberate difference (no authored toolchain-first ruling here, unlike Laksa). |
| `baize which [tool]`          | opt-in + `cmd/which`            | The PATH-walk toolchain report (report/gate split from `check toolchain`; always exits 0). Catalogue ships the name (D22); the handler is the port.                                                        |
| `baize cv <probe> <frame>`    | `cmd/cv`                        | Tier-1 auto handler: ORIGINAL_CWD captured before cd so relative frame paths resolve against the CALLER's directory; routes to `devbin cli bz.cv.<probe>`.                                                 |
| `baize perf guard/bench/baseline` | `cmd/perf`                  | Tier-1 auto: guard execs the mix runner with the LOAD-BEARING `--include perf` + the three paths; bench/baseline via cli (`bz.cv.bench`); baseline warns before overwriting the tracked fixture.           |
| `baize db ...`                | `cmd/db`                        | Full shadow: setup (deps.get + rack_task_sub setup -- avoids the root `mix setup` alias and says why), migrate [--test] (ash.migrate, subprocess), codegen <name> (in-process rack_task, name mandatory), reset [--test], seed, proxy (STUB exit 3). |
| `baize fmt [paths] [--check]` | catalogue fmt.elixir            | `mix format` -- exact match. `fmt --check` retired into `check format` (D21, the fleet rename). **`fmt md` DISABLED in config** (`enabled: false`): Baize's authored ruling -- markdown is deliberately not wired into fmt, do not add without a ruling. |
| `baize docs ...`              | `cmd/docs`                      | Full shadow -- the surface is Baize's own: `index <dir>` (its NAME for treeindex, explicit dir, root banned), `completions` (rack_task baize.completions), `agents`, `all` = agents + completions (never index). The root-ban guard ports from Baize's own file. |
| `baize publish [docset]`      | opt-in + `cmd/publish`          | Thin pass-through to `docs/bin/publish` (docset table stays there). Catalogue ships the name (D22).                                                                                                       |
| `baize build <target>`        | `cmd/build`                     | The four `not_yet` stubs (release/deploy/nif/firmware), each exit 3 with its gating condition -- a build that exits 0 having built nothing is the false green the gates exist to refuse.                    |
| `baize version ...`           | catalogue @builtin + defaults   | `version_from` defaults to VERSION -- no entry at all. No sidecars (mix.exs READS the file; nothing to write). set/bump output wording differs (devbin's); sync/check are additions.                       |
| bare `baize` / `-v`           | dispatcher                      | Bare -> full help, exit 0 (parity). `-v` -> `baize <version>` ✓.                                                                                                                                          |
| unknown command               | dispatcher                      | Both exit 2 (the Laksa probe generalises: devbin's rc-1 ruling covers BARE commands only).                                                                                                                |

## Languages: the activation call

Baize's Intent config declares `[elixir, swift, rust, shell]`; devbin's `languages:` is the GATE ACTIVATION key (D11) and deliberately declares `[elixir, shell]`. Declaring rust would activate `check clippy` + catalogue cargo rows against a tree with NO Cargo.toml ("no Rust in the tree yet" -- test rust's own stub text) -- new reds the old launcher never produced; swift likewise has no source tree. The old launcher's own answer to rust is the stub, and the stub ports. The day ST0005 Phase 3 lands the first crate, adding `rust` here lights the catalogue arms -- that is the designed path. `check critic` is unaffected either way: it reads the INTENT declaration directly, both sides, so all four critics run.

## Options

`env` and `json` declared (`MIX_ENV`; `ARCA_STYLE` via the flag-with-value form -- the reference config's own cited example); `--iex` is D20 framework-owned. Same anywhere-in-argv difference as Laksa, same exposure argument to probe (no baize task declares --env/--json/--iex switches).

## Shims and entry points -- the switch-day map

- `bin/bz` is a SYMLINK to `baize` (lstat-verified; an earlier cmp read through the link and called it a copy -- corrected). It rides the switch with NO edit: bz -> baize -> devbin chains, and the dispatcher resolves through the chain.
- `bin/cli` and `bin/repl` exec `baize_cli` / `baize_repl` DIRECTLY -- they would dangle when the family is deleted. At the switch they are RETARGETED to route through the dispatcher (`exec "$(dirname "$0")/baize" cli "$@"`), which is what Laksa's shims already did by construction. Two-line edits, in the switch commit, verified live before it.
- `bin/completions/completions.txt` stays at its old path (cmd/repl names it; `docs completions` regenerates it).
- `test/shell/helpers_test.sh` SOURCES `bin/baize_helpers` -- its subject. Pre-switch it correctly gates the OLD machinery (old is canonical). IN the switch commit its source line moves to the vendored `bin/.devbin/lib/{helpers,runlog}` (same function names by lineage; `init_run_colors` -> `init_colors`; grammar globals -> `grammar_for`), so the project keeps a local gate on the sealing machinery its verdicts actually rest on -- vc's original ask. `test shell` re-runs green post-switch as part of the switch verification. `assert_test.sh` is self-contained and rides unchanged.

## Toolchain sweep (hv's standing directive)

- NO Dockerfile, no fly.toml, no release config -- there is no image arm to sweep and nothing to registry-verify. This is the negative data point for AC-11.11.
- `.tool-versions` already at the fleet pins (erlang 29.0.5, elixir 1.20.3-otp-29, landed 2026-08-09) and its authored comment block -- a ruling document (declaration-not-mechanism, the one-home policy, the deliberate rust non-pin) -- is PRESERVED byte-for-byte; the sweep changes nothing here.
- CI (.github/workflows/ci_cd.yml) greps both versions from `.tool-versions` and hard-fails when the file is absent -- NO fallback copies exist (verified lines 63-88). Nothing to bump.

## Help

15 authored topics migrate verbatim (help-migration.md rules 1, 4, 5), rulings extracted first: the agent ban (server), the seal doctrine + LATEST_* warning + zero-test promotion (test), the report/gate split (which), the `--include perf` load-bearing note (perf), the umbrella gotcha + deprecation trap (db), the no-markdown ruling (fmt), the re-baseline discipline (perf), the stub policy (build). The global heredoc dies; its fragments land in help.tagline, the group annotations, and option summaries. Baize's pre-commit hook is the Intent critic chain ONLY -- no prettier pass -- but `.prettierrc.json` (proseWrap never, printWidth 9999) exists for manual runs and `bin/` is not excluded by `.prettierignore`, so every topic is proven `npx prettier --check` clean under the project's own config before its first commit.

## Project dirt, surfaced not carried silently

- `db reset` runs the root `mix setup` alias -- the alias whose deprecated `mix cmd --app` spelling `db setup` deliberately avoids and documents avoiding. The port carries it VERBATIM (a faithful shadow) and this line surfaces it for hv: aligning reset with setup's direct two-step form is a one-line Baize-side fix, not the migration's to make.

## Old-side gates, verbatim, for the equivalence pack

`test mix` (glyph feed; equivalence runs are SUITE-SCOPED -- `test suite marker` etc. -- because the bare full suite is forbidden by the same standing rule the runner enforces), `test credo` (--strict, whole project), `test shell` (the bash suites), `test rust` (stub, rc 3 both sides), `check {compile,format,deps,toolchain,critic,credo}`, `which` (rc 0 + drift restatement), seals under tmp/test with lowercase suffixes. Old-side reds expected today: none known; `check toolchain` should be green on both (pins match the active toolchain) -- if it is red, it is red on both sides with the same facts.
